business_scope.primary_industry_name: Interactive Language Education and Automated Tutoring Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (unitary national; corporate statutes modeled on the Delaware General Corporation Law; RMI constitutional and customary law does not override corporate registry requirements)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: No bilateral investment treaty is currently in force for the Republic of the Marshall Islands.
No comprehensive double taxation agreement is currently in force for the Republic of the Marshall Islands.
Amended Compact of Free Association with the United States of America (2023) contains economic assistance and investment-related provisions but is not a BIT or a standard FTA.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Business Corporations Act 1990, as amended, Title 27 Marshall Islands Revised Code (MIRC), Chapter 1, including registered agent and corporate records obligations; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2012, as amended, and related Financial Intelligence Unit regulations and directives; RMI Registrar of Corporations directives on beneficial ownership and customer due diligence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the RMI Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade if the destination state is an Apostille Convention contracting state; otherwise consular legalization through an RMI embassy or consular officer.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Existence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, depending on the recipient jurisdiction; certified by the registered agent after issuance.
Notarization by an RMI notary public followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization, as required by the destination state.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized shareholder and director resolutions approving incorporation and authorizing the registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Shareholders, directors, and RMI notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in the jurisdiction of signature, followed by Hague Apostille or RMI consular legalization, as applicable.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO and AML/CFT due diligence declaration and source of wealth/records pack
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed RMI registered agent / RMI Financial Intelligence Unit-compliant compliance officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature page and certification; forwarded under registered agent cover for government or bank countersignatory use.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed directors, shareholders, 25%+ beneficial owners, signatories, and commercial counterparties against the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit sanctions and restriction notices, the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, FATF high-risk jurisdiction lists, and adverse media/reputational risk sources. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), including family members and close associates, require enhanced due diligence and senior management approval where the PEP holds 5% or more of the capital or exercises control. Any sanctions hit, unexplained source of wealth, or false UBO declaration is disqualifying at pre-incorporation stage unless a valid OFAC/UN license or national exemption is obtained.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands - Corporate Name Reservation Portal and Online Registry Filing System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered corporate name must be in the Latin/Roman alphabet and must be expressed in English. Non-English names must be transliterated into Roman characters and accompanied by an English translation. The Registrar will reject names containing punctuation, special symbols, or misleading script forms. Marshallese diacritical marks are accepted only where the name is rendered in a recognizable Latin script.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected name may be administratively reconsidered by the Registrar upon written request submitted by the applicant or licensed registered agent within 14 days of the rejection notice. The request must cite the proposed name, the statutory ground for rejection, and a corrected or distinguishing element. If the Registrar affirms rejection, an appeal may be filed in the High Court of the Republic of the Marshall Islands within 30 days. A reservation may be renewed once for an additional 30-day period before expiry if no competing application exists; after expiry, a new name reservation application must be filed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office at the licensed RMI registered agent's registered address satisfies the statutory registered-office and service-of-process requirement for this non-resident EdTech business corporation, provided the agent maintains a physical street address in Majuro and accepts process. No separate physical operational office in the Marshall Islands is required for the ISIC 6201 software subscription activity, and the business is not licensed as a regulated financial institution.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated unannounced physical inspection probability is 2-5% per year for an EdTech subscription entity with no regulated financial license, no physical RMI operations, no government procurement exposure, and no adverse AML/CFT alert. The probability rises above 10% if the entity later begins processing virtual currency, payment aggregation, or cross-border remittance activity without proper licensing.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed registered agent and registered office service - first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for RMI non-resident business corporations; includes service of process acceptance and statutory records custody.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a low-risk EdTech software subscription structure with a single corporate owner and clear source of funds.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for standard incorporation package; includes digital copy and registered agent certificated copies.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act of 1990 (as amended), Republic of the Marshall Islands Revised Code Title 51, principally Sections 54-58 (Articles of Incorporation), 63 (Registered Office), and 69 (Subscribers); Business License Act 2008, Title 33.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Marshall Islands Business Registry (MIBR), Office of the Attorney General, Majuro Atoll
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form BC-1), submitted through an MIBR Accredited Registered Agent
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a non-resident business corporation; subscribers may issue no-par shares for unpaid consideration; no escrow or segregated deposit account is mandated under the Business Corporations Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation adopts its Articles of Incorporation and the Bylaws presented to this Board; RESOLVED, that the subscription for 1,000 non-assessable shares by the founding subscriber is hereby accepted, no paid-up capital being required, and no escrow account being mandated; RESOLVED, that the registered office at the Agent's address in Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands, and the appointment of the registered agent are confirmed; RESOLVED, that the following officers are appointed to serve at the pleasure of the Board: President, Secretary, and Treasurer; RESOLVED, that the corporate seal is adopted and any executive officer is authorized to open bank accounts and execute contracts in the Corporation's name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Marshall Islands Business Registry (MIBR), Office of the Attorney General, electronic name reservation platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the Accredited Registered Agent to submit one preferred and two alternative corporate names; pay the name reservation fee; obtain the Certificate of Name Reservation confirming the name is distinguishable under Section 54 of the Business Corporations Act.
required_dossiers: Proposed legal name (one primary and two alternatives)
Brief statement of corporate purpose (EdTech subscription software)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity, the agent may file a written response within 15 business days or reserve an amended name; no state fee is charged for the initial refile.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Articles of Incorporation and Registered Agent Consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MIBR Accredited Registered Agent and notarizing officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporator executes the Articles of Incorporation stating corporate name, duration, authorized share structure (including no-par shares), registered office located in Majuro, and the name and address of the resident registered agent; the registered agent executes a formal consent to serve.
required_dossiers: Registered agent consent and registered office acceptance
Draft Bylaws for initial director adoption
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a Defective Filing Notice, the agent executes an Articles of Correction or refiles the defective page within 14 business days without additional registry fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: E-Filing of Articles of Incorporation and Statutory Fee Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, MIBR, Majuro (filing portal operated through accredited agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Articles via the MIBR electronic filing portal; attach proof of name reservation and the registered agent consent; pay the USD 350 official fee plus the agent statutory charge; obtain the registry docket number and time-stamped acknowledgement.
required_dossiers: E-filed Articles of Incorporation with manifests
Fee payment debit authority or receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried for incomplete schedules or inconsistent capitalization, the agent files a supplemental affidavit curing the defect; the applicant receives 21 business days from the query notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Kit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After validation, the Registrar endorses the Articles and issues the Certificate of Incorporation dated as of the statutory filing date; the registered agent assembles the corporate minute book, seal, and share certificate jackets.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains clerical variance, the entity presents the original to the Registrar for administrative rectification within 10 business days at no charge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board of Directors Organizational Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Business Corporation, clerked by the Accredited Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold an organizational meeting or act by unanimous written consent to adopt the Bylaws, accept the share subscription, appoint the President, Secretary, and Treasurer, fix the registered office and agent, adopt the corporate seal and banking resolution, and confirm no escrow account is required.
required_dossiers: Notice of meeting or unanimous written consent of directors
Subscription agreement and share issuance ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any irregularity in the organizational resolution is cured by a subsequent unanimous written consent of the directors ratifying the initial acts within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business License and Post-Incorporation Statutory Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenue and Taxation Office, Ministry of Finance and Banking, and Economic Policy, Planning and Statistics Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the General Business License application under the Business License Act 2008 with the prescribed revenue-band fee; register for employer withholding if staff will be engaged; file the non-resident ownership declaration (100% non-resident ownership permitted); open a Majuro bank account for investor contributions and subscription proceeds.
required_dossiers: Business License application (Form BL-1) specifying on-line education software subscription activity
Registered office and registered agent confirmation
Employer tax registration form (IR-044), if applicable
Annual franchise tax payment schedule (USD 200 base)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the license application is deferred for missing premises or financial attestation, the applicant supplements the file through the registered agent; the Revenue and Taxation Office will adjudicate within 14 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Revenue and Taxation Office, Ministry of Finance and Banking
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General Business License (Business License Act 2008) for On-Line Software and Digital Content Subscription Services

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI EPA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (Category C - administrative and office activity; no construction, manufacturing, or waste discharge)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not triggered for pure software operations; where office space is occupied, sanitary wastewater must comply with Majuro municipal sewer ordinances, e-waste must be deposited at RMI EPA collection depots, and any backup generator must meet EPA noise and particulate emission thresholds; no Full EIA Report is required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance from the Majuro Fire and Rescue Services; structural and electrical inspection by the Majuro Atoll Local Government building inspector; workplace safety alignment with Ministry of Health and Human Services guidelines and workers' compensation coverage under the RMI Workers' Compensation Act for any local employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Marshall Islands Revenue and Customs Administration (RMI RCA) / Division of Revenue and Taxation, Ministry of Finance, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands. Official national e-services portal: https://rmigov.info; customs and excise declaration portal: https://www.rmicustoms.org.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: File Articles of Incorporation with the Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro, electing status as a Non-Resident Domestic Corporation under the Business Corporations Act 1990 (BCA); no minimum capital is required and 100% foreign ownership is permitted. Step 2: Obtain the Certificate of Incorporation carrying the statutory MH registration number; this number functions as the corporate identifier / TIN-equivalent for the entity. Step 3: Appoint a registered agent and maintain a registered office in the Marshall Islands; file an Annual Report and pay the annual franchise/registration fee to the Registrar of Corporations. Step 4: No TIN or tax-registration application to the RMI Revenue and Customs Administration is required for a tax-exempt non-resident company; the entity is statutorily exempt from RMI income, gross revenue, stamp, franchise, and capital taxes. Step 5 (conditional): register with the RMI Customs Division for an importer code only if physical goods are imported into RMI, and obtain a Ministry of Finance Business License only if a physical place of business, retail, or trading activity is established within RMI. For pure offshore EdTech subscription activities (ISIC 6201 - Interactive Language Education and Automated Tutoring Software), Steps 1 through 3 are exhaustive; Steps 4 and 5 are not triggered.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The Marshall Islands does not adopt the United States check-the-box regime and does not administer OECD hybrid-mismatch or hybrid-payment elections. The operative statutory election is the entity-status election under the Business Corporations Act 1990: (i) election in the Articles of Incorporation to register as a Non-Resident Domestic Corporation, which confers tax-exempt-zone treatment and prohibits carrying on domestic business with RMI resident persons; versus (ii) election to operate as a Domestic Corporation, which is subject to Title 18 RMI Code gross revenue tax on RMI-source activity. The election is made at incorporation, is evidenced by the Certificate issued by the Registrar of Corporations, and does not require annual re-election; the board may additionally adopt a bylaws election confirming the non-resident operational restriction.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No_VAT_GST_Sales_and_Use_Tax_Regime - the Marshall Islands levies no value-added, goods-and-services, or retail sales tax; the only indirect-type impositions are customs import duty on physical imports and, solely for domestic non-exempt entities, the gross revenue tax under Title 18 RMI Code.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not_Applicable - no VAT/GST registration threshold exists because no VAT or GST is imposed; the currency of account is the United States Dollar (USD). A customs importer code is required from the first physical import into RMI with no monetary de minimis threshold, and a Ministry of Finance Business License is required only where the entity maintains a physical presence or sells goods/services within RMI. Offshore digital export of EdTech language-learning subscriptions does not trigger any indirect-tax registration threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. The Marshall Islands imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing, SAF-T, digital stamping, or tax-authority API reporting on EdTech subscription revenue. Payments collected through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing are outside any RMI fiscal reporting or clearance channel. Physical-goods imports are declared electronically to the RMI Customs Division under a declaration-based control model; export of digital services requires no fiscal clearance whatsoever.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Formally not applicable: because RMI has no VAT/GST regime, cross-border EdTech subscription supplies do not bear any RMI indirect tax, and no zero-rating claim, certificate, or export-status approval is required. Digital exports (remote language tutoring platforms, automated learning assessment, subscription e-learning software) are extraterritorial to the Marshall Islands and remain outside the gross revenue tax base even for domestic corporations, which is assessed only on RMI-source business activity.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (required only for physical goods exported from RMI; not applicable to EdTech digital services)
Commercial_Invoice_and_Subscription_Revenue_Report (contractual audit trail for EdTech subscription revenues)
Inward_Remittance_Certificate_or_Bank_Credit_Advice (USD remittance/collection proof where bank-level documentary evidence is required)
Payment_Rails_Settlement_Statements (Apple IAP and Google Play Billing settlement reports retained for revenue-recognition and transfer-pricing audits)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Because no VAT is levied, there is no export zero-rating and no VAT refund/clawback-recovery procedure to enforce. The principal audit risks for the MH Business Corporation are: (1) loss of tax-exempt status if the RMI Revenue and Customs Administration determines that the entity carried on prohibited domestic business or prohibited resident activities, triggering retrospective revocation of the exemption and reassessment to gross revenue tax, interest, and penalties under Title 18 RMI Code; (2) false or incomplete declarations to the RMI Customs Division, which attract forfeiture, monetary penalties, and potential criminal sanctions under the Customs Acts; (3) failure to file annual reports or pay Registrar franchise fees, which results in administrative dissolution and reinstatement penalties; and (4) the 180-day repatriation deadline is not a statutory RMI exchange-control rule because the US Dollar is legal tender and RMI maintains no foreign-exchange controls; the deadline operates as a covenant in underlying subscription-financing agreements and is enforceable contractually, not through tax clawback.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banking Commissioner, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands (no central bank exists; U.S. dollar is the sole legal tender)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Marshall Islands uses the U.S. dollar as domestic legal tender and maintains no independent exchange-control regime. Both capital and current account transactions are freely convertible, and there are no statutory obstacles to profit remittance, dividends, or repatriation of contributed capital. The practical friction is limited to anti-money-laundering and OFAC sanctions screening by correspondent banks in the U.S. clearing system. A non-resident-owned Business Corporation must maintain good standing with the Registrar and file annual reports; however, no exchange-control license or central-bank approval is required for remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export-proceeds surrender rules exist. Because USD is the domestic currency, export receipts are not subject to mandatory conversion, nor is there a statutory timeline for remittance or surrender to a designated account. Exporters are free to retain proceeds in any USD-denominated account; the only obligations are bank record-keeping and suspicious-transaction reporting under the Republic of the Marshall Islands Banking Act and anti-money-laundering regulations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium. The RMI has no distinct Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licensing category. Offshore digital EMIs are not recognised as banks or licensed payment institutions; they cannot accept deposits or provide settlement accounts within RMI without a banking licence. They may be used only as ancillary payment cards or e-wallet interfaces, provided the underlying settlement account is held at an RMI-licensed bank and all transactions are channelled through that bank. OFAC and correspondent-bank restrictions make purely offshore EMI onboarding unreliable for corporate treasury.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person director appearance is the baseline requirement at Bank of Marshall Islands and Bank of Guam for non-resident corporate accounts. Remote opening is only permitted for existing clients or with pre-approval, executed via a qualified notary in a recognised jurisdiction and legalised/apostilled documents; the final sign-off still requires a physical interview by a local compliance officer or an accredited overseas representative. Directors are therefore expected to appear personally for the initial risk-based interview or provide a fully compliant proxy with a certified power of attorney.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident corporate client with opaque beneficial ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Registry extract, full beneficial-ownership chart signed by each director, trust/ownership deed, apostilled corporate resolutions, passport copies, and a specific written explanation of the EdTech subscription business model.

Three months of bank statements from the originating entity, audited financial statements of the shareholder, signed share-purchase/contribution agreement, tax invoices or subscription-revenue records from the EdTech platform, and a cash-flow projection in USD.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction pattern mismatch with expected turnover
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed payments-flow diagram covering Apple-IAP/Google-Play settlement, holding-company reconciliation ledger, monthly subscription-revenue reports, and the executed contract with the payment facilitator.
OFAC screening certificates, end-user declarations, export/import records, IP/territory access logs, and legal counsel opinion confirming no sanctioned-party nexus.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity contributions must be wired in USD via SWIFT MT103 using the bank's correspondent network, typically through a U.S. Fedwire/CHIPS correspondent bank. The remitter must include a precise payment narrative: 'Equity contribution to [Entity Name], Business Corporation, no goods/services'. The beneficiary bank will verify the corporate name, account number, and entity standing; a certified copy of the board resolution authorising the capital injection and a share issuance certificate should be submitted to the RMI bank before the first credit to a Capital Escrow Account. Funds are not released for operational purposes until the escrow account is converted to an Operational Account after final AML/KYC sign-off.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade payments for software licensing, infrastructure, and marketing services settle in USD via SWIFT MT103 or a Commercial Letter of Credit subject to UCP600. MT103 is used for direct supplier payments with invoice/contract references encoded in field 70. A Commercial LC is appropriate when the supplier requires a bank undertaking; the issuing bank in RMI will instruct a U.S. correspondent bank or advising bank. All disbursements must match the declared business purpose, preserve a six-year record, and pass OFAC screening; payments to sanctioned jurisdictions are blocked.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright USD/EUR forward contracts (non-deliverable and deliverable) with a licensed international bank
Currency swaps on USD/JPY/GBP/AUD via ISDA documentation
NDFs on covered emerging-market currencies only for settlement of cross-border vendor invoices

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report of the Business Corporation (director, officer, registered agent and registered office details) filed under the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act 1990, s.108; filing fee scale: US$300 for authorized capital up to US$50,000 and US$500 for authorized capital above US$50,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands (Majuro)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before the last calendar day of the month in which the anniversary of incorporation falls (e.g., 31 March for a March-incorporated corporation); no extension is available
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late-filing surcharge of 10% of the unpaid annual report fee accrues for each year or part thereof of delinquency; failure to file or pay for more than twelve months after the due date permits the Registrar to administratively strike off the corporation, with reinstatement conditioned on settlement of all arrears, surcharges and a statutory reinstatement fee

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent Annual Compliance Confirmation and Beneficial Ownership / Controller Data Refresh (agent-administered record, not submitted to the Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Marshall Islands registered agent; the retained record is subject to lawful inspection by the Registrar and RMI financial-intelligence authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days after the annual report anniversary date and within 14 days of any share transfer or change in ultimate beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No statutory fine; continued non-response permits the registered agent to resign on 30 days' notice. If the corporation fails to appoint a replacement licensed agent, the Registrar may strike off the corporation for lack of a registered agent

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Records Update (written consents or minutes of directors and shareholders and inspection-ready statutory registers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company minute book and statutory registers held at the registered office in the Marshall Islands
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months of the previous annual meeting; written consents in lieu of meetings must be recorded within 30 days of execution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No Registrar filing penalty; deficient records constitute a breach of fiduciary duty by directors, expose the corporation to shareholder inspection and court-order remedies, and prejudice evidentiary positions in litigation

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Nil for a non-resident private EdTech business corporation. The RMI Business Corporations Act 1990 imposes no mandatory statutory audit; an audit is required only when mandated by the corporation's articles or bylaws, by a board or shareholder resolution, or by lender or investor arrangements. The audit mandate of the RMI Securities Act 2019 applies solely to public issuers and is inapplicable to a private subscription EdTech entity.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No statutory accounting standard is prescribed; the corporation must keep books of account in US dollars reflecting its transactions and financial condition. IFRS, or alternatively US GAAP, is the accepted framework for RMI non-resident corporations and should be selected by the board and applied consistently.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The RMI has no public UBO register. The licensed registered agent must collect, verify and retain the corporation's beneficial-ownership and controller data. The corporation must inform the agent of any share transfer or ownership change within 14 days, and the agent circulates an annual confirmation for certification by the directors. The records are confidential but must be made available to the Registrar or competent RMI authorities upon lawful demand.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$750 - US$1,500 per year for a licensed Marshall Islands registered agent, inclusive of registered-office services, annual report preparation, and UBO record maintenance
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not statutorily required; where demanded by investors or payment-platform partners, a proportionate independent audit of a small subscription EdTech entity typically ranges US$4,000 - US$10,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (non-resident domestic corporation exemption from income tax on foreign-source income)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: RMI Taxation: Non-resident domestic corporations under Business Corporations Act Section 108 are exempt from all RMI income tax on income derived outside the Marshall Islands. No capital gains tax, no withholding tax, no branch profits tax, and no gross receipt tax applies to foreign EdTech subscription revenue. Only an annual registry license fee is payable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Not applicable — no RMI income tax return is imposed on an exempt non-resident domestic corporation. The sole annual filing obligation is the Annual Corporate Report (Form 108) filed through the Marshall Islands Corporate Registry e-Registrar online portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No tax return deadline under RMI law for exempt non-resident domestic corporations. The Form 108 annual report must be filed within 30 days after the anniversary of incorporation, irrespective of the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the exact name from the Certificate of Incorporation; indicate 'non-resident domestic corporation' status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal office address and mailing address
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign street address required; do not list a P.O. Box in the Marshall Islands as the principal office.
List all directors with foreign addresses; the registered agent must be a licensed RMI service provider.
Enter amounts in U.S. dollars; no minimum capital is required, but the annual license fee is calculated from authorized capital.
Certify that no commercial activity has taken place within RMI and no RMI-source income was earned; attach the annual exemption certificate if requested.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year-end and annual accounts confirmation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm the fiscal year-end; financial statements need not be filed under RMI law, but maintain records for ESR and AML review.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 10% per month of the annual license fee, capped at 100%; failure for more than 12 months leads to administrative dissolution; reinstatement requires payment of all arrears plus a reinstatement fee of USD 1,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% (RMI does not impose dividend withholding tax on distributions by a non-resident domestic corporation)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: RMI has no comprehensive double tax treaty network; no treaty relief process is applicable. Where a foreign tax authority requires proof of RMI non-resident status, the Registrar will issue a Certificate of Non-Resident Status and, upon written application to the RMI Tax Office accompanied by the certificate of incorporation, annual report filing receipt, and non-resident status declaration, a Tax Residency Certificate may be issued. Such certificate does not create treaty benefits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate: 0% on royalties and interest paid to non-residents. Treaty rate: 0% / N/A (no DTA network).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No RMI-stipulated monetary threshold for mandatory Local File or Master File. Because non-resident domestic corporations are taxed at 0%, the RMI transfer pricing regime is limited to the arm’s length standard for RMI-source income; a practical threshold of USD 1,000,000 in intercompany controlled transactions is recommended for contemporaneous documentation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Yes. The Economic Substance Regulations 2020 apply. An EdTech language-learning entity holding or exploiting IP (including software rights and an online tutoring platform) conducts a relevant activity (IP business). It must maintain an RMI economic substance profile: board meetings with a quorum in RMI, principal direction and management in RMI, full-time employees and physical premises adequate to the IP activity, core income-generating activities in RMI, and an annual ESR notification filing. A pure holding activity may rely on a reduced substance requirement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Exemption Claim
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deriving revenue from RMI sources or maintaining a permanent physical presence in Majuro while filing the Section 108 non-resident exemption certificate, or knowingly omitting related-party controlled transactions from records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of gross revenue at 3% of RMI-source receipts; fraud penalty of 100%; interest at 0.75% per month; a fine not exceeding USD 50,000 or twice the evaded tax; imprisonment up to 5 years under the Income Tax Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced under common law fraudulent purpose; directors may be jointly and severally liable for tax, penalties, civil restitution, travel bans, and a term of imprisonment up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a pure IP-holding scheme for the EdTech language software without any real management or employees in RMI; appointing nominee directors who do not meet or make decisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ESR annual penalty of USD 10,000 to USD 20,000 for the first year; USD 50,000 for a continuing default; the Registrar may strike off the company and the non-resident tax exemption may be revoked.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false ESR declarations face fines, disqualification from serving as directors, and travel bans; restitution may be ordered for any foreign tax advantages obtained.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to conduct customer due diligence in high-volume digital subscription flows from Apple/Google IAP, especially in chargeback disputes or suspicious refund routing, or failing to appoint an AML compliance officer.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to USD 5,000,000 and imprisonment up to 20 years for money laundering under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2003; corporate assets may be restrained and frozen.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers face criminal liability, civil forfeiture, and travel bans; refusal to repatriate illicit funds may lead to extradition or an Interpol red notice.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fraudulent Transfer / Transfer Pricing Red Flag
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Excessive royalty payments from an operating subsidiary to the MH BC without an arm’s length study, with no actual substance, resulting in foreign operating company insolvency and lower foreign tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Foreign tax authorities may recharacterize the royalty as a dividend, disallow a deduction, apply withholding taxes and penalties typically in the range of 20% to 40%; RMI provides no shelter from such foreign ruling.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the beneficiary entity may be ordered to provide civil restitution to creditors, be disqualified, and, if fraudulent intent is shown, imprisoned up to 7 years with travel bans.
